notes: The whole 28-page PDF, read end to end: the historical context, the synthesis for the Sunset District and then the Oceanside itself (the early community, Carville, the earthquake refugee shacks, the neighbourhood name, the 1909 street renaming, well water and piped water, the improvement clubs, schools and churches), the property types and architectural styles, SPEAK's goals and priorities, both parts of the methodology, the bibliography and all 51 endnotes. Pages 12 and 13 are full-page maps and carry no text. The document is laid out in two columns, which `pdftotext -layout` interleaves line by line — every page was re-extracted one column at a time before reading, and five addresses are invisible to a regex over the interleaved text. There is no appendix inventory: the survey this statement accompanies produced 511 DPR 523 A forms, 60 B forms and 5 district forms, and none of them are in this file. The endnotes are the richest single seam — four of the findings here come from them. Addresses that appear solely as somebody's home are not recorded, per the privacy limits in the root AGENTS.md; builders, developers, contractors and the people two houses are named for are named in their building role, which the same rule permits.

coverage.remaining: None of this document. The Part Two DPR 523 A/B/D forms it describes — 511 properties surveyed, 60 documented in depth, 5 potential districts — are a separate corpus and are not held here.
coverage.note: Read 28 pages and found 32 address-level facts, 28 of them carrying a street number across 27 distinct number-and-street pairs, all in the outer Sunset west of 37th Avenue. Four are recorded with no street number because the statement identifies a block face rather than a building: the Craftsman rows on the 1200 blocks of 42nd, 37th and 41st Avenues and the row of five on the 1600 block of the Great Highway. Never candidates, and so not recorded: eleven buildings the statement locates only by cross street (the Ocean Side House on the Great Highway between Ulloa and Vicente, St. Andrews-by-the-Sea on 47th Avenue near Irving, St. Paul's Presbyterian Church on Kirkham between 46th and 47th and later at 43rd and Judah, the Oceanside Primary School on 43rd between Irving and Judah, the Oceanside Electric Light Company plant on 47th near Kirkham, the Oceanside and Park News at 48th and Judah, the Oceanside Pharmacy at the north-west corner of 48th and Judah, the Spring Valley water tower on 41st near Lincoln Way, the Barefoot Club's streetcar clubhouse at 46th and Lawton, Sol Getz's branch office at 47th and Lincoln Way, and Col. Dailey's shack at Lincoln Way and the Great Highway); one cover photograph that gives a number but asserts nothing datable (1247-49 46th Avenue); and one address that appears only as a named person's home.

findings.address_as_written: 1632 Great Highway
findings.description: The last known streetcar house in San Francisco — two streetcars and a horse car, the pair of them raised to a second storey. Built in 1908, when the beach settlement of cast-off railway cars known as Carville was already being burned and cleared by neighbours who thought it held property values down. Every other car house here is gone.

findings.address_as_written: the Joseph Keith residence at 1648 Great Highway (1908)
findings.description: Built in 1908, and picked out as a very fine example of the Classical Revival in a neighbourhood where the style is uncommon — columns, pilasters, pediments and layered window mouldings, against the shingled cottages all around it.

findings.address_as_written: Houses at 1231 42nd Avenue
findings.description: One of a row of fifteen Craftsman houses Alonzo Harrington built along this block between 1911 and 1913 — one of only two long rows put up in the neighbourhood before 1915, and the work of the one builder here the survey rates above local scale. The row is largely intact, and this house has been restored, with earlier unsympathetic modernisations reversed.
